responses.text: {"images":[{"id":1,"description":"Figure 2. Line chart titled Percentage of 3- to 4-year-olds and 5-year-olds enrolled in school: October 2010 through October 2021. The vertical axis is Percent from 0 to 100 and the horizontal axis is Year from 2010 to 2021. A solid dark green line labelled 5-year-olds stays near 90 percent from 2010 through 2019 (about 92 percent in 2010 and 91 percent in 2019), falls to about 84 percent in 2020 and recovers to about 86 percent in 2021. A dashed dark green line labelled 3- to 4-year-olds stays near 53 to 54 percent from 2010 through 2019, drops to about 40 percent in 2020 and rises to about 50 percent in 2021. A note states that data exclude children living in institutions; the source is the Census Bureau Current Population Survey, October 2010 through 2021, Digest of Education Statistics 2022, table 202.20.","page":20,"position":"middle","type":"chart","educationalPurpose":"Shows that preprimary enrollment rates were stable before the pandemic, fell sharply in October 2020 for both age groups and only partly recovered by October 2021."},{"id":2,"description":"Figure 3. Line chart titled Enrollment in public elementary and secondary schools, by level: Fall 2010 through fall 2021. The vertical axis is Enrollment, in millions, from 0.0 to 60.0 and the horizontal axis is Year from 2010 to 2021. A black line labelled Total runs from about 49.5 million in 2010 up to about 50.8 million in 2019, then drops to about 49.4 million in 2020 and 2021. A dark green line labelled Prekindergarten through grade 8 runs from about 34.5 million to about 35.6 million in 2019, then falls to about 34.1 million in 2020 and 34.0 million in 2021. A pale green line labelled Grades 9 through 12 rises slowly from about 15 million to an all-time high of about 15.4 million in 2021. Footnote 1 says grades 9 through 12 include students reported as enrolled in grade 13; notes explain that totals cover the 50 states and the District of Columbia, include traditional public and public charter schools, prorate ungraded counts and include imputations for California and Oregon. Source: NCES Common Core of Data, State Nonfiscal Survey of Public Elementary/Secondary Education, 2010-11 through 2021-22, Digest of Education Statistics 2022, table 203.10.","page":21,"position":"middle","type":"chart","educationalPurpose":"Shows that the pandemic-era drop in total public school enrollment came from prekindergarten through grade 8 while grades 9 through 12 kept growing."},{"id":3,"description":"Figure 4. Line chart with markers titled Enrollment in elementary and secondary schools, by school type: Selected years, fall 2010 through fall 2021. The vertical axis is Enrollment, in millions, from 0.0 to 50.0 and the horizontal axis is Year from Fall 2010 to Fall 2021. A solid dark green line with square markers labelled Traditional public stays near 47 million from 2010 through 2019 (47.4 million in 2010) and drops to about 45.4 million in 2020 and 2021. A dashed dark green line with triangle markers labelled Private, plotted for odd years 2011 through 2019, stays near 4.5 to 4.7 million. A pale green line with diamond markers labelled Public charter rises steadily from about 1.8 million in 2010 to about 3.7 million in 2021. Notes explain that traditional public and public charter enrollments include prekindergarten while private school enrollment covers kindergarten through grade 12 only. Source: NCES Common Core of Data Public Elementary/Secondary School Universe Survey 2010-11 through 2021-22 and Private School Universe Survey 2011-12 through 2019-20, Digest of Education Statistics 2021 table 205.20 and Digest 2022 table 216.20.","page":22,"position":"top","type":"chart","educationalPurpose":"Shows that public charter school enrollment more than doubled between fall 2010 and fall 2021 while traditional public school enrollment declined and private school enrollment stayed flat."},{"id":4,"description":"Figure 5. Grouped bar chart titled Percentage distribution of student enrollment in public elementary and secondary schools, by race/ethnicity: Fall 2010 and fall 2021. The vertical axis is Percent from 0 to 100 and the horizontal axis is Race/ethnicity with seven groups. Each group has a dark green bar for Fall 2010 and a light green bar for Fall 2021, with the value printed above each bar: American Indian/Alaska Native 1 and 1; Asian 5 and 5; Black 16 and 15; Hispanic 23 and 28; Pacific Islander # and # (rounds to zero); White 52 and 45; Two or more races 2 and 5. Footnote 1 says fall 2021 includes imputations for nonreported prekindergarten enrollment in California and Oregon; the note explains that data cover the 50 states and the District of Columbia, race categories exclude persons of Hispanic ethnicity, and rounded figures may not sum to 100. Source: NCES Common Core of Data, State Nonfiscal Survey of Public Elementary and Secondary Education, 2010-11 and 2021-22, Digest of Education Statistics 2022, table 203.50.","page":23,"position":"top","type":"chart","educationalPurpose":"Shows how the racial and ethnic composition of public school students shifted between fall 2010 and fall 2021, with the White and Black shares falling and the Hispanic and Two or more races shares rising."}]}
